cards.claim: Uniform circular motion is motion along a circular path at constant speed.
cards.quote: When an object follows a circular path at a constant speed, the motion of the object is called uniform circular motion.

cards.claim: In uniform circular motion the acceleration has magnitude v^2/R and always points toward the centre (centripetal acceleration).
cards.quote: Thus, the acceleration of an object moving with speed v in a circle of radius R has a magnitude v2/R and is always directed towards the centre.

cards.claim: Angular speed omega is the time rate of change of angular displacement.
cards.quote: We define the angular speed ω (Greek letter omega) as the time rate of change of angular displacement :

cards.claim: Speed and angular speed are related by v = omega R, and the centripetal acceleration is ac = omega^2 R.
cards.quote: It is related to velocity v by v = ω R. The acceleration is ac = ω 2R.

cards.claim: The net acceleration in circular motion points to the centre only if the speed is constant; otherwise it is not purely centripetal.
cards.quote: The resultant acceleration of an object in circular motion is towards the centre only if the speed is constant.

cards.claim: NCERT Example 3.9: an insect in a 12 cm radius groove makes 7 revolutions in 100 s; find angular and linear speed, and whether the acceleration is a constant vector.
cards.quote: An insect trapped in a circular groove of radius 12 cm moves along the groove steadily and completes 7 revolutions in 100 s. (a) What is the angular speed, and the linear speed of the motion? (b) Is the acceleration vector a constant vector ? What is its magnitude ?

cards.claim: In NCERT Example 3.9 the angular speed is 2 pi x 7/100 = 0.44 rad/s and the linear speed is 0.44 s^-1 x 12 cm = 5.3 cm/s.
cards.quote: ω = 2π/T = 2π × 7/100 = 0.44 rad/s The linear speed v is : v =ω R = 0.44 s-1 × 12 cm = 5.3 cm s-1

cards.claim: Centripetal acceleration has constant magnitude but is not a constant vector, since its direction keeps changing to point at the centre.
cards.quote: Since v and R are constant, the magnitude of the centripetal acceleration is also constant. However , the dir ection changes — pointing always towards the centre. Therefore, a centripetal acceleration is not a constant vector.

cards.claim: NCERT Exercise 3.14: a stone on an 80 cm string whirled in a horizontal circle makes 14 revolutions in 25 s; find the magnitude and direction of its acceleration.
cards.quote: A stone tied to the end of a string 80 cm long is whirled in a horizontal circle with a constant speed. If the stone makes 14 revolutions in 25 s, what is the magnitude and direction of acceleration of the stone ?

cards.claim: NCERT Exercise 3.16: true or false - net acceleration in circular motion is always radial; velocity is always tangent to the path; the average acceleration over one cycle of uniform circular motion is null.
cards.quote: Read each statement below carefully and state, with reasons, if it is true or false : (a) The net acceleration of a particle in circular motion is always along the radius of the circle towards the centre (b) The velocity vector of a particle at a point is always along the tangent to the path of the particle at that point (c) The acceleration vector of a particle in uniform circular motion averaged over one cycle is a null vector

cards.claim: NCERT Exemplar 4.14 asks which statements about a particle in uniform circular motion are correct.
cards.quote: For a particle performing uniform circular motion, choose the correct statement(s) from the following: (a) Magnitude of particle velocity (speed) remains constant. (b) Particle velocity remains directed perpendicular to radius vector. (c) Direction of acceleration keeps changing as particle moves. (d) Angular momentum is constant in magnitude but direction keeps changing.
